title: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head N (Ministry of Foreign Affairs)

sections.label: US-China strategic rivalry tensions
sections.summary: Relations grew tense as strategic rivalry developed, with a US bipartisan consensus on being tough on China, a 2018 trade war with tariffs, and bifurcation of technology and supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In the last decade though, relations have grown more tense as a strategic rivalry has developed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: There is now a bipartisan consensus in the US that they need to be "tough" on China.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: This resulted in a trade war in 2018 – with both slides slapping tariffs on goods from each other and with pressure on businesses to disengage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The current tensions have already led to a bifurcation of technology and supply chains.

sections.label: Export restrictions and friend-shoring
sections.summary: Large powers imposed restrictions on exports of raw materials and technology and began using friend-shoring and near-shoring to bring critical supply chains closer to home.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: The large powers have imposed restrictions on their exports of raw materials and technology and have begun to use "friend-shoring" and "near-shoring" to bring critical supply chains closer to home.

sections.label: Singapore as AI thought-leader
sections.summary: Singapore should position itself as a thought-leader on AI and play a constructive role in developing international rules governing AI use and development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Singapore should work to position ourselves as a thought-leader on AI; and play a constructive role in the development of international rules that will govern the use and development of AI.

sections.label: Singapore in Operation Prosperity Guardian
sections.summary: Singapore is participating in Operation Prosperity Guardian, a US-led initiative to restore maritime shipping through the Red Sea, and supported UN Security Council Resolution 2722 condemning Houthi attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Singapore is participating in Operation Prosperity Guardian (OPG), a US led initiative to restore free flow of maritime shipping through the Red Sea and rebuild confidence in trade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
sentences.text: Singapore supported the adoption of the UN Security Council Resolution 2722 on 10 January 2024 which condemned the Houthi attacks "in the strongest terms" and demanded that the Houthis cease all attacks on merchant and commercial vessels.

sections.label: Singapore humanitarian aid for Gaza
sections.summary: Singapore voted at the UN for immediate humanitarian ceasefire resolutions and sent humanitarian goods for Gaza to Al Arish, Egypt, and deployed a SAF medical team on a French Navy ship.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: At the UN, Singapore has consistently voted in favour of resolutions calling for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: The Government has also cooperated with like-minded partners to provide humanitarian assistance.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: It has worked with partners like the Singapore Red Cross and Mercy Relief to send humanitarian goods for Gaza on the RSAF's Multi-Role Tanker Transport to Al Arish, Egypt, in November 2023.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong (West Coast)
sentences.text: Just last month, SAF deployed a medical team to treat injured civilians from Gaza on board a French Navy Ship.

sections.label: Singapore work with small nations
sections.summary: The question asks for updates on Singapore's 2024 initiatives with small nations through platforms like Small Island Developing States, FOSS, 3G and the Alliance of Small Island States, and how it will engage and assist them on challenges like climate change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can the Ministry provide updates on Singapore's planned initiatives in 2024 in its work with other small nations through platforms, such as the Small Island Developing States, the Forum of Small States (FOSS), 3G and the Alliance of Small Island States.

sentences.speaker: Ms Usha Chandradas (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In particular, can the Minister explain how Singapore is planning to engage with and assist these groups to prepare for common challenges, such as that of climate change?

sections.label: Areas for countries to cooperate
sections.summary: The passage states there are many areas for countries to cooperate, including low-carbon and renewable energy technologies, carbon capture and storage and carbon credits.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Going forward, there are many areas for our countries to cooperate in, such as the sharing of low-carbon and renewable energy technologies, carbon capture and storage and carbon credits.

sections.label: Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone
sections.summary: The passage states that the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) is one such example.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: One such example is the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ).

sections.label: Update on cooperation with Malaysia
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the Minister can provide an update on the state of cooperation with Malaysia, including Johor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Could the Minister kindly provide an update on our state of cooperation with Malaysia, including Johor?

sections.label: Indonesia presidential election result
sections.summary: The passage states Indonesia held its presidential election on 14 February 2024 and Defence Minister Prabowo Subianto won a convincing majority.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Indonesia held its presidential election on 14 February 2024 and Defence Minister Prabowo Subianto won a convincing majority.

sections.label: Indonesia in ASEAN and economy
sections.summary: The passage states Indonesia is the largest country in ASEAN and the world's 16th largest economy, achieving 5% GDP growth in 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Indonesia is also the largest country in ASEAN and the world's 16th largest economy, achieving a GDP growth of 5% in 2023.

sections.label: Green-Digital Partnership with Vietnam
sections.summary: The passage states a Green-Digital Economic Partnership with Vietnam was signed in February 2023 and Conditional Approvals were issued to import low-carbon electricity from Cambodia and Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: In February 2023, we signed a Green-Digital Economic Partnership with Vietnam to strengthen collaboration in the green and digital economies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: The Energy Market Authority has also issued Conditional Approvals to import low-carbon electricity from Cambodia and Vietnam.

sections.label: Expanded Framework agreements signed ratified
sections.summary: Both countries have signed and ratified the three agreements under the Expanded Framework covering airspace, defence and extradition.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Both our countries have signed and ratified the three agreements under the Expanded Framework, which covers key issues, such as airspace, defence and extradition.

sections.label: Support for Laos and Timor-Leste
sections.summary: Singapore should support Laos' ASEAN Chairmanship and is training Laotian officials and supporting Timor-Leste's ASEAN accession roadmap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: We should render all possible support for Laos' ASEAN Chairmanship this year – just as we did for previous years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: I am pleased to note that MFA is providing training courses for Laotian officials under the Singapore-Laos Enhanced Cooperation Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: Singapore is also supporting Timor-Leste in its efforts to fulfil the roadmap for its accession to ASEAN.

sentences.speaker: Mr Keith Chua
sentences.text: For instance, our Singapore-Timor-Leste ASEAN Readiness Support package provides support for capacity-building.

sections.label: Scam increase and losses
sections.summary: The Straits Times reported a 46.8% increase in scams in 2023, with losses totalling $651.8 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The Straits Times recently reported – based on Police figures – 46.8% increase in scams in 2023, with loss totalling $651.8 million.

sections.label: MFA Myanmar engagement plans
sections.summary: MFA stated it will safeguard interests through engaging stakeholders and supporting ASEAN's peaceful resolution efforts, prompting a question on concrete plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
sentences.text: The MFA stated at page 104 of the FY2024 Revenue and Estimates regarding Myanmar, "We will safeguard our interests through engagement of all key stakeholders, while playing a constructive role in supporting ASEAN's efforts to encourage a peaceful resolution to the crisis." So, what are MFA's concrete plans for playing this constructive role?

sections.label: Economic cooperation trading partners
sections.summary: On economic cooperation, the countries are each other's largest trading partners, outweighing China and the US.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: With regard to economic cooperation, we are collectively each other's largest trading partners – outweighing both China and the US.

sections.label: Myanmar, South China Sea, Mekong issues
sections.summary: Examples include Myanmar negotiation difficulties, South China Sea dispute management, and Mekong River erosion and riparian issues.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some prime examples, include Myanmar and the difficulties in promoting negotiations among the warring parties; the South China Sea, especially how to promote peaceful management of disputes; and addressing erosion and other riparian issues along the Mekong River.

sections.label: Investing in institution budget
sections.summary: Changes may include investing in the institution, such as increasing the Secretariat's budget and capacities to perform its mandate more efficiently.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Changes may include, for instance, investing in the institution, such as by increasing the budget and capacities of the Secretariat to ensure that it can perform its current mandate more efficiently and effectively.

sections.label: Singapore Qatar and Oman visits
sections.summary: Singapore hosted the 8th Qatar-Singapore High-Level Joint Committee in August 2023, and Oman's Sultan made a first-ever State visit in December 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In August 2023, Singapore hosted the 8th Qatar-Singapore High-Level Joint Committee, which Qatar Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Sheikh Mohammed Bin Abdulrahman Al Thani and Senior Minister Teo Chee Hean co-chaired.

sentences.speaker: Mr Neil Parekh Nimil Rajnikant (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: In December 2023, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik made the first-ever State visit by an Oman Sultan to Singapore.

sections.label: Singapore-China partnership upgrade
sections.summary: Prime Minister and Chinese President Xi Jinping upgraded Singapore-China relations to an All Round High-Quality Future-Oriented Partnership in March 2023.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Chairman, Prime Minister and Chinese President Xi Jinping upgraded relations between Singapore and China to an "All Round High-Quality Future-Oriented Partnership" in March 2023.

sections.label: China-Singapore economic ties
sections.summary: China is Singapore's top merchandise trading partner, while Singapore is China's largest foreign investor.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: On the economic front, China is our top merchandise trading partner while Singapore is China's largest foreign investor.

sections.label: Wong China JCBC visit
sections.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Wong co-chaired the 19th JCBC in China, concluding 24 deliverables including the CSFTA Further Upgrade Protocol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister Wong had a successful visit to China last December to co-chair the 19th Joint Council for Bilateral Cooperation (JCBC) with Vice Premier Ding Xuexiang, concluding 24 deliverables across a broad range of sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: For instance, we announced the signing of the China-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (CSFTA) Further Upgrade Protocol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Shawn Huang Wei Zhong (Jurong)
sentences.text: There were also deliverables in areas like green, digital, finance, and food security cooperation.

sections.label: US-China rivalry economic ties
sections.summary: Shifts driven by US-China rivalry and nationalism have consequences, prompting questions on Singapore's economic ties and partnership with the US.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: These major shifts are driven by the heightened US-China rivalry, which many of my colleagues spoke about, as well as the rise of nationalism, isolationism and sharp divisions within parts of the American electorate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: These shifting views have real consequences for us as the US. has and continues to be our largest source of cumulative foreign direct investments and advanced technology.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: As such, can MFA provide an update on our economic ties with the US?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
sentences.text: Can MFA also share how Singapore can remain a trusted partner to the US and ensure that we continue to be open to US investment and business?

sections.label: Relations with China
sections.summary: A question asks the Ministry about plans to maintain relations with China and deepen a strategic partnership beyond traditional economic realms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Amidst these major changes, I would like to ask the Ministry about our plans to maintain our relations with China and deepen a strategic partnership which extends beyond traditional economic realms.

sections.label: External influence on national identity
sections.summary: Concerns about a charm offensive targeting overseas ethnic Chinese and Indians raise questions on how MFA ensures Singaporeans foster a strong national identity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: As major global players, there are concerns about their efforts to project a "charm offensive" targeting ethnic Chinese and Indians living overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: This raises important questions for Singapore: How does MFA ensure that Singaporeans continue to foster a strong national identity in the face of these external influences?

sections.label: COVID-19 supply chain vulnerabilities
sections.summary: Global crises such as COVID-19 have exposed the vulnerabilities of global supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Global crises, such as COVID-19, have exposed the vulnerabilities of global supply chains.

sections.label: Supply chain resilience for food and energy
sections.summary: A question asks how MFA supported efforts to strengthen Singapore's supply chain resilience, especially for food and energy, amid worries about weaponised supply chains.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Countries are increasingly worried that others may weaponise critical supply chains for political leverage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: We must adapt to an evolving world and find new ways to diversify our supply chains, especially for critical commodities such as food and energy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How has MFA supported efforts to strengthen Singapore's supply chain resilience, especially in the areas of food and energy?

sections.label: Sharing experiences with developing countries
sections.summary: For more than 30 years, it has been an important avenue for Singapore to share experiences and support capability building in developing countries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: For more than 30 years, it has been an important avenue for Singapore to share our experiences and support capability building in developing countries.

sections.label: Consular services post COVID-19
sections.summary: The Minister anticipated greater demand for consular services post COVID-19 and said MFA will meet it through technology and professional first responders.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: In the Addendum to the President's Address in April 2023, the Minister anticipated a greater demand for consular services post COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: He also signalled that MFA will meet this increased demand by harnessing technology and through a new corp of professional first responders trained to provide 24/7 consular response to Singaporeans.

sections.label: World more dangerous place
sections.summary: The passage states that the world has become an even more dangerous place.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: First, the world has become an even more dangerous place.

sections.label: Russia Ukraine war, US China rivalry
sections.summary: It describes the Russia-Ukraine war entering its third year and continuing deep US-China strategic rivalry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Last year, I spoke of a "perfect storm of multiple interlocking crises".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The war between Russia and Ukraine is headed into its third year, and the meat grinder, the casualties mount on both sides and there is no end in sight.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Tensions between the US and China have calmed somewhat at a tactical level, but the deep strategic rivalry, the lack of strategic trust continues apace.

sections.label: Israel and Hamas conflict
sections.summary: It states that the conflict between Israel and Hamas is the latest addition to a litany of woes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, the tragic conflict between Israel and Hamas is the latest addition to this litany of woes.

sections.label: Calling out international law violations
sections.summary: It says Singapore opposed Russia's Crimea annexation in 2014 and condemned Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And what this means is being prepared to stand up and call out all violations of international law whenever, wherever it happens, and even if it displeases some of our stakeholders and some of our partners or even neighbours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This was why we opposed Russia's annexation of Crimea in 2014 and we condemned Russia's invasion of the Ukraine in 2022.

sections.label: Operation Prosperity Guardian contribution
sections.summary: It says Singapore contributed personnel to Operation Prosperity Guardian against what it assesses as unlawful Houthi attacks on commercial shipping.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Again, I am trying to make the point that we take a position for our long-term national interest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: That is why we contributed personnel to the multinational Operation Prosperity Guardian to protect freedom of navigation and to protect the key sea lines of communication in response to what we assess to be unlawful attacks on commercial shipping by the Houthis.

sections.label: Singapore's long-term national interest
sections.summary: It states Singapore will not be any power's pawn and will choose based on its long-term national interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: When many people asked us about United States and China, implicit in their comments or the question is which side are you going to take?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will not become anybody's cat's paw or pawn or Trojan horse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will be useful; but we will not be used by any other power.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will look at issues as and when they come up dispassionately and we will always choose on the basis of Singapore's long-term national interests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But will we need to stand firm and to be prepared from time to time to say no – not in a gratuitous and provocative way but because they know we have done our own calculations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We take a stand, based on our assessment of our long-term national interest.

sections.label: Singapore's global partnerships and anniversaries
sections.summary: Singapore maintains equities with major powers and marked 30 years of the Suzhou Industrial Park and 20 years of the US-Singapore FTA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: That has enabled us to maintain good and significant equities with both the United States, China, Russia, Europe and all the middle emerging powers – Australia, India, Africa, South America.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This year, we celebrated the 30th anniversary of the Suzhou Industrial Park – our first government-to-government project with China.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This year is also the 20th anniversary of the US-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (FTA), the first FTA that United States signed with an Asian country.

sections.label: Condemnation of Russia's invasion
sections.summary: Singapore condemned Russia's invasion of Ukraine as a clear violation of international law.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Russia's war with Ukraine was, in fact, a precursor, a preamble for us.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We took the position to condemn Russia's invasion because it was a clear violation of international law.

sections.label: Economic impact of Ukraine war
sections.summary: The war in Ukraine had significant economic impact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The war in Ukraine had significant economic impact.

sections.label: Gaza humanitarian crisis
sections.summary: The fighting in Gaza has resulted in an appalling humanitarian crisis.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The fighting in Gaza has resulted in a humanitarian crisis that is appalling.

sections.label: Condemnation of 7 October attack
sections.summary: Singapore condemned Hamas's 7 October attack on civilians and hostage-taking as a blatant, abhorrent act of terrorism that cannot be justified.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But what happened on 7 October – and I know I have had this debate with the Leader of the Opposition before – we had to condemn that specific episode on 7 October, when Hamas launched an attack on civilians and took hostages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: This was a blatant and abhorrent act of terrorism, which cannot be justified by any circumstance, context, historical reason or justification.

sections.label: Call for Gaza humanitarian ceasefire
sections.summary: Singapore says Israel's military response has gone too far and calls for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire in Gaza, voting for two UN resolutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, Israel's military response has gone too far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The catastrophic situation in Gaza demands an immediate humanitarian ceasefire to alleviate the unbearable suffering of the civilian victims and to enable humanitarian assistance to reach them immediately.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have made our position clear, both in my conversations with Israel and all our Arab friends and partners, and at the UN.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We voted for the two UN General Assembly resolutions on the protection of civilians and upholding legal and humanitarian obligations, which called for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire.

sections.label: Singapore international relations engagement
sections.summary: Singapore manages international relations by staying engaged with the international community and maintaining ties with willing countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Well, I need to tell everyone that we manage our international relations by remaining engaged with the international community and maintaining ties with as many countries as possible that are willing to maintain ties with us.

sections.label: Israel and Palestine right to exist
sections.summary: Both Israel and Palestine have a right to exist, with Israel living securely and Palestinians having a homeland.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Both Israel and Palestine have a right to exist.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Israel has a right to live peacefully within secure borders, but the Palestinian people also have a right to a homeland.

sections.label: Singapore backs negotiated two-state solution
sections.summary: Singapore believes a negotiated two-state solution consistent with UN Security Council Resolutions 242 and 338 is the only basis for durable peace.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: There is so much distrust and animosity and the recent events have only made things worse.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: But for what it is worth, I tell all our friends and partners in the Middle East that Singapore continues to believe that a negotiated two-state solution, consistent with UN Security Council Resolutions 242 and 338, is the only possible basis for a durable peace.

sections.label: Singapore raises Gaza relief funds
sections.summary: Singaporean NGOs and the Government raised more than $10 million for relief operations to Gaza so far.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Singaporean non-government organisations (NGOs) and the Government raised more than $10 million for relief operations to Gaza so far.

sections.label: Third tranche aid through Jordan
sections.summary: Singapore and Jordan's Foreign Minister agreed to donate a third tranche of aid for Gaza, working through Jordan.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: I told Members just now I spoke to the Jordanian Foreign Minister last night.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We have agreed that we will donate a third tranche of aid for Gaza and, this time, we will work through Jordan.

sections.label: Warning against Singapore splitting
sections.summary: If Singapore splits and polarises on affinity, history, identity, race, language or religion, it will be divided, weaker, vulnerable and not independent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Everything will come to bear at the same time, both the economic and the emotional impact.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: And if that happens, if Singapore splits, polarises, divides on the basis of affinity or history or identity, race, language or religion, we will be sunk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: We will be divided, we will be weaker, we will be vulnerable, we will not be independent, we will not have autonomy.

sections.label: Chief Rabbi and Mufti solidarity
sections.summary: The Chief Rabbi and Mufti publicly showed solidarity, calling for stronger Jewish-Muslim bonds and praying for long-term peace, despite criticism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Where else in the world can you get the Chief Rabbi and the Mufti come together in the immediate aftermath of a horrendous attack and a catastrophic response?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: Where else in the world will the Rabbi and the Mufti come together in a public display of solidarity, call for stronger bonds between the Jewish and Muslim communities and express their hope and prayers for long-term peace?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: The Mufti and the Chief Rabbi have both come in for criticism.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Vivian Balakrishnan)
sentences.text: They are people who have stood up – not just for their communities – but have made Singapore a stronger, safer, better place.

sections.label: Singapore position on conflict
sections.summary: Singapore voted for two UN General Assembly resolutions and called for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire to help affected civilians.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore has clearly stated our position towards this conflict.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: This includes our votes in favour of two UN General Assembly (UNGA) resolutions last October and December.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Singapore has also called for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire, so that assistance can be effectively rendered to all affected civilians.

sections.label: Two-state solution belief
sections.summary: Singapore firmly believes a two-state solution consistent with relevant UN Security Council resolutions is needed for lasting peace.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To achieve a lasting peace settlement, Singapore firmly believes that a two-state solution consistent with the relevant UN Security Council resolutions is needed.

sections.label: Gaza relief and Palestinian Authority support
sections.summary: Over S$10 million was raised for Gaza relief, and Singapore will continue supporting Palestinian Authority capacity building through a S$10 million package.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Between the Government and the public, we have raised more than S$10 million to support relief efforts in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In the long term, we will continue our long-standing support for the Palestinian Authority’s capacity building efforts through our S$10 million Enhanced Technical Assistance Package (ETAP).

sections.label: Malaysia trade and links
sections.summary: Malaysia was a top three trading partner with $123.6 billion bilateral trade, an MOU on the Johor-Singapore SEZ was signed, and the RTS Link will operate by 2026.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Malaysia was one of our top three trading partners last year – with bilateral trade hitting $123.6 billion.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For instance, we signed an memorandum of understanding (MOU) on the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (SEZ) last month.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: By 2026, the new Rapid Transit System Link (RTS) will be operational – facilitating more cross-border interactions.

sections.label: Indonesia Expanded Framework Agreements
sections.summary: Singapore worked closely with President Joko Widodo's administration and signed and ratified the Expanded Framework Agreements, resolving long-standing bilateral issues.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have worked closely with President Joko Widodo's administration over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We signed and ratified the landmark Expanded Framework Agreements, turning the page on a generation of long-standing bilateral issues.

sections.label: Singapore-Indonesia tech and food cooperation
sections.summary: The programme will let young tech professionals from Singapore and Indonesia work in each other's countries, and Singapore has imported live chickens from the Riau Islands since May 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: When launched, the programme will allow young tech professionals from Singapore and Indonesia to work in each other's countries and gain exposure.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We made good progress in food security cooperation, with Singapore importing live chickens from the Riau Islands since May 2023.

sections.label: Singapore support for Timor-Leste ASEAN accession
sections.summary: Singapore is stepping up engagement to support Timor-Leste's ASEAN accession preparations and plans to open a resident Embassy in Timor-Leste.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To Mr Keith Chua's query about Timor-Leste, we are stepping up our engagement to help support their preparations to join ASEAN, following ASEAN's adoption of the Roadmap for Timor-Leste's accession in May last year.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have also announced our plans to open a resident Embassy in Timor-Leste.

sections.label: ASEAN economy and workforce
sections.summary: ASEAN has 660 million people, a young workforce, urbanisation and healthy GDP growth, and is the fifth largest economy, possibly fourth by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: With 660 million people, a young workforce, urbanisation and healthy GDP growth, ASEAN is already the fifth largest economy in the world and could be the fourth largest by 2030.

sections.label: Power integration and low-carbon electricity imports
sections.summary: Singapore looks forward to enhancing the LTMS-PIP and has issued Conditional Approvals to import low-carbon electricity from Indonesia, Cambodia and Vietnam.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: On our part, we look forward to enhancing the pilot Lao PDR-Thailand-Malaysia-Singapore Power Integration Project (LTMS-PIP), which serves as a pathfinder for the potential grid.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We have issued Conditional Approvals to import low-carbon electricity from Indonesia, Cambodia, and Vietnam.

sections.label: Singapore support for Laos ASEAN chairmanship
sections.summary: Singapore is committed to giving Laos full support for its ASEAN chairmanship, including through the Singapore-Laos Enhanced Cooperation Package.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: To Mr Neil Parekh's query, we are committed to giving Laos our full support for their ASEAN chairmanship, including through the Singapore-Laos Enhanced Cooperation Package.

sections.label: Singapore-India youth and cooperation ties
sections.summary: Singapore will explore knowledge sharing between Singaporean and Indian youths and cooperation through the India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable, and had high-level exchanges with Middle Eastern countries.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Given our close people-to-people ties, we are keen to explore opportunities to promote knowledge sharing between Singaporean and Indian youths through platforms like the Asia-Ready Exposure Programme or the ASEAN-India Exchange Programme.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We will also explore cooperation through the India-Singapore Ministerial Roundtable in areas like fintech, sustainability and food and energy security.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In the past year, we have had several high-level exchanges with Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Oman, Egypt and Jordan.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: We established a Strategic Partnership with Saudi Arabia during Prime Minister's visit in October last year, our first in the region.

sections.label: Prime Minister official visits
sections.summary: The Prime Minister made his first official visits to South Africa and Kenya in May 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For instance, Prime Minister made his first official visits to South Africa and Kenya in May 2023.

sections.label: Ambassador Rena Lee BBNJ agreement
sections.summary: Ambassador Rena Lee oversaw the conclusion of the BBNJ international agreement in March 2023, supporting Singapore's role on law of the sea.

sentences.speaker: The Second Minister for Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: For instance, Ambassador Rena Lee oversaw the successful conclusion of the international agreement on Marine Biodiversity of Areas Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) in March 2023, buttressing Singapore's leading role on international law of the sea issues.

sections.label: Singapore condemns Hamas attack
sections.summary: Singapore strongly condemned Hamas' attack on and killing of Israel civilians and kidnapping of hostages on 7 October 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singapore has strongly condemned Hamas’ attack on and killing of Israel civilians and the kidnapping of hostages on 7 October 2023.

sections.label: Israel Gaza humanitarian ceasefire call
sections.summary: After recognising Israel's right to self-defence, Singapore insisted Israel comply with international humanitarian law and called for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire in Gaza.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: After the 7 October attacks, we recognised Israel’s right to self-defence.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: If Singapore is ever attacked, we would certainly exercise this right to self-defence – indeed, our duty is to protect our citizens.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: However, we have consistently insisted that Israel comply with international humanitarian law.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, Israel’s military response has gone too far.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The catastrophic situation in Gaza demands an immediate humanitarian ceasefire to alleviate the unbearable suffering of the Palestinian civilian victims and enable humanitarian assistance to reach them.

sections.label: Singapore-China relations upgrade
sections.summary: In 2023 Singapore-China relations were upgraded to an All-Round High-Quality Future-Oriented Partnership, with over 20 deliverables announced at the 19th JCBC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Bilateral cooperation is deep and multifaceted. 2023 saw the upgrade of Singapore-China relations to the unique status of an “All-Round High-Quality Future-Oriented Partnership”.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: During the 19th JCBC last year, more than 20 deliverables were announced.

sections.label: Singapore US security trade ties
sections.summary: Singapore is the US' only Major Security Cooperation Partner, with bilateral trade more than doubled in 20 years and the US its largest foreign investor.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Singapore is the US' only Major Security Cooperation Partner.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Bilateral trade has more than doubled since its entry into force 20 years ago.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Today, the US is our largest foreign investor, top trading partner in services and third-largest partner in goods trade.

sections.label: US presence in region
sections.summary: The US presence and leadership is seen as vital for the region's stability, security and prosperity, and the US is encouraged to engage through IPEF.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Our long-held view is that the US' presence and leadership has played and will continue to play a vital role for the stability, security and prosperity of the region.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Foreign Affairs (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We will continue to encourage the US to engage the region through initiatives like the Indo Pacific Economic Framework (IPEF).

sections.label: US-China relationship
sections.summary: The US-China relationship is described as the most consequential in the world and one being watched closely.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The US-China relationship is the most consequential one in the world and one that we are watching closely.

sections.label: Deepening Europe relations
sections.summary: Relations with Europe are being deepened, and the UK was welcomed as the CPTPP's newest member in July 2023.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We are also deepening our relations with Europe.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We welcomed the UK as the CPTPP's newest member in July 2023.

sections.label: Digital Trade Agreement
sections.summary: Work will go towards concluding an ambitious and modern Digital Trade Agreement to increase bilateral trade and model an ASEAN-EU-wide agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For example, we will work towards the conclusion of an ambitious and modern Digital Trade Agreement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: When completed, it will increase bilateral trade and serve as a model for an eventual ASEAN-EU-wide digital trade agreement.

sections.label: Foreign policy begins at home
sections.summary: Singapore's foreign policy begins at home, so MFA will keep engaging the public on Singaporeans' concerns and explaining foreign policy.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: It is truly the case that Singapore's foreign policy begins at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: This is why MFA will continue engaging the public to understand Singaporeans' concerns and to explain our foreign policy.

sections.label: PAP position on event
sections.summary: The Minister said the PAP's position was not to attend the event because it was organised for only one race of MPs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Minister shared with me, at least the PAP's position was they would not be going for this event because of the particular way it was organised – only for one particular race of MPs to show up.

sections.label: Cutting relations with Israel
sections.summary: A view existed that Singapore should cut relations with Israel, and the current Israeli leadership does not believe in the two-state solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But there was a view that we should cut relations with Israel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But it will be helpful to understand the nuance of how foreign policy is determined when you have a situation where one party, for example, does not believe in the two-state solution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The current Israeli leadership does not believe in the two-state solution.

sections.label: Public understanding of foreign policy
sections.summary: Some public understanding of how Singapore moves vis-à-vis its own position would be helpful, including on sanctioning Russia.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: The Minister again may have experienced it and he spoke about it in his speech, where insofar as the Russia-Ukraine conflict is concerned, individuals are asking why do we go so far as to sanction Russia, when we can actually make our point by saying we disagree with their actions towards Ukraine because this goes against international law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: So, some understanding for the public about how we move vis-à-vis our own position would be helpful.

sections.label: Private talks and Gaza agreement
sections.summary: The Minister affirms private and sensitive conversations with the Opposition, consensus on a particular issue, and agreement that 7 October was terror and there is a right of self defence.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: He has revealed a private and sensitive conversation that we had.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I am not going to go through the details, but I do want to affirm that, yes, I do have private and sensitive conversations with the Opposition.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I will also affirm that to date, in fact, we have arrived at consensus, we have arrived at agreement, specifically for that particular issue, but I would also say, as a matter of habit, we have been able to make sure our politics stop at the water's edge – and for that, I thank you.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The next thing, since a lot of the Member's questions have been about the problems in Gaza, I am going to start – and I welcome you to correct me if I am wrong – by listing where we agree.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I think I have heard the Member say he agreed that what happened on 7 October was an act of terror.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The Member has also affirmed that there is a right of self defence.

sections.label: Diplomatic ties with disagreeing governments
sections.summary: The Minister suspects the Member agrees Singapore should not sever diplomatic ties even when another country's government disagrees on policy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Specifically, for the Member's on diplomatic ties – and I think we both received the same emails – I detect in the Member's question — actually, I suspect the Member actually agrees with me that we should not sever diplomatic ties, even when the government of the day of another country may have quite a fundamental disagreement with us on policy.

sections.label: No broken ties in 59 years
sections.summary: The Minister does not think Singapore has ever broken ties in 59 years, or in the Prime Minister's 20 years.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Specifically, for diplomatic ties – and I stand ready to be corrected by the Prime Minister – I do not think we have ever broken ties in 59 years or at least in the 20 years that the Prime Minister has been around.

sections.label: No broken ties with Russia
sections.summary: In the case of Russia and Ukraine, Singapore has not broken ties with Russia.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: To add on examples to that, in the case of Russia and Ukraine, we have not broken ties with Russia.

sections.label: Targeted sanctions and arms controls
sections.summary: Singapore levies targeted, not bilateral, sanctions and ensures it is not a portal for arms or dual-use equipment usable against Ukrainians.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It is not personal, it is not bilateral, and even when we go as far as to levy sanctions, these are targeted sanctions.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: We will make sure that Singapore is not a portal for arms or dual-use equipment which can be used against Ukrainians and Ukrainian civilians.

sections.label: Singapore's say on Israel-Palestine
sections.summary: Singapore has no say in what will happen between Israel and Palestine.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In this case, Singapore has no say in what will happen between Israel and Palestine.

sections.label: Foreign policy differences not dividing Singaporeans
sections.summary: The aim is not Middle East peace but that Singaporeans with different deeply held opinions are not divided.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: What we are trying to achieve here is not peace in the Middle East, but for us, all Singaporeans, we are able to say we may have different opinions, deeply held for a variety of reasons, but it will not divide us.

sections.label: Thanks for foreign policy consensus
sections.summary: The speaker thanks the Leader of the Opposition, Opposition Members and NMPs for consensus on foreign policy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: For that, I thank the Leader of the Opposition, I thank the Members of the Opposition and the NMPs for what I believe today is consensus on foreign policy.

sections.label: MFA consular cases and evacuations
sections.summary: In 2023 MFA handled 4,419 consular cases, issued 1,535 Documents of Identity, and worked with other governments to evacuate Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In 2023, MFA handled 4,419 consular cases and facilitated the issuance of 1,535 Documents of Identity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: With diplomatic representation in just 56 countries, a constant challenge we face is how to provide assistance where we do not have a ground presence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: For example, we worked with the Republic of Korea to help evacuate five Singaporeans from Tel Aviv to Seoul in October.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We also partnered the Thai, Vietnamese and Chinese governments to evacuate Singaporeans from northern Myanmar last year.

sections.label: Consular case management system
sections.summary: A consular case management system digitally connects overseas missions and headquarters to track cases and coordinate assistance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We are also embracing technology to help improve the quality of our services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have developed a consular case management system that connects our overseas missions and headquarters digitally, which allows us to better track consular cases and better coordinate the provision of assistance to Singaporeans.

sections.label: Ceasefire and hostage release
sections.summary: Singapore voted for an immediate humanitarian ceasefire and says hostages taken on 7 October should be released completely, immediately and unconditionally.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: More specifically for this issue, we have said we voted for immediate humanitarian ceasefire.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I should also have added that actually the hostages taken on 7 October should be released, should be released completely, immediately and unconditionally.

sections.label: EU agreements and Germany ties
sections.summary: Singapore works with EU member states to ratify the ESPCA and Investment Protection Agreement, and pursues green and digital cooperation with Germany.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: On the ratification of the ESPCA – that is what we call it, EU-Singapore Partnership and Cooperation Agreement – as well as Investment Protection Agreement, we are constantly working with the EU member states to have these agreements ratified because we negotiated them together and we believe that these are very important agreements that will complement the EU-Singapore FTA in bringing about greater certainty for our companies on both sides and also at the same time enhance the cooperation that we have at all levels with the EU.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: As for Germany, we in fact are pursuing cooperation in emerging areas such as the green and digital economies with many partners, Germany is one of them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: But I am happy to share with the Member that we have a very strong foundation with Germany because we have already welcomed more than 2,200 German companies to Singapore which have created more than 4,500 jobs here.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I have a clarification for Minister for Foreign Affairs on Israel.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I understand that late last year, Singapore appointed a resident ambassador to Israel and it was the first time that Singapore actually has a resident ambassador there despite having diplomatic ties with Israel for more than 50 years.

sections.label: Singapore Cooperation Programme capacity building
sections.summary: Singapore shares development experiences through the SCP, which has trained over 150,000 officials, and has a Sustainability Action Package.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In terms of our support of other countries' capacity building efforts, this is something that we are committed to.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We want to be constructive partners in supporting the development of other countries, because we recall how Singapore has benefited from the assistance of others during the early years of our Independence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: So, we do this by sharing our development experiences through the Singapore Cooperation Programme, or SCP for short.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: In the last 30 years, over 150,000 officials from more than 180 countries, territories and inter-governmental organisations have participated in SCP in a wide range of capacity‑building courses, among which we are giving greater focus to sustainability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: We have a Sustainability Action Package, or SAP, which supports efforts by developing countries to build resilience in water and food security, to manage and finance green projects and to develop sustainable infrastructure and carbon markets.

sections.label: Pacific resilience assistance package launch
sections.summary: The launch of the Singapore Pacific Resilience and Knowledge Sharing Technical Assistance Package was announced during the meeting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: During the meeting, we announced the launch of the Singapore Pacific Resilience and Knowledge Sharing Technical Assistance Package.

sections.label: Retail diplomacy for MFA
sections.summary: MFA staff must do far more retail diplomacy, explaining diplomacy domestically and deploying ambassadors to schools and institutions of higher learning.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: In the case of MFA, I have told my staff and they all agree with me, we have to do far more of what we call retail diplomacy.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: Meaning diplomacy is no longer just travelling, meeting, engaging your counterparts, but we have to make the case back home domestically and explain it.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: It means every ambassador is not just an ambassador overseas, but I have told my ambassadors every time they come back for mid-term consultations or for meetings, we will have to deploy them in schools, in universities, institutions of higher learning.

sections.label: ASEAN informal assistance networks
sections.summary: Within ASEAN, Singapore reaches out informally through ASEAN networks to help citizens, including evacuations where it joined convoys led by ASEAN neighbours.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: The final point I will make, and this also relates to ASEAN, we have a very good informal but functional relationship within ASEAN, that even when our people or citizens need help and we do not have a mission on the ground, informally, we reach out through our ASEAN networks to provide assistance.

sentences.speaker: Dr Vivian Balakrishnan
sentences.text: I should record my thanks that there have been even occasions when evacuating Singaporeans from war zones, we have had to "tompang" convoys led by or organised by our ASEAN neighbours.
